intervals.label: data taking
intervals.note: Month precision for the start, from the collaboration member's page. Dore (EPJ H 37, 2012) writes 'took data from 1977 in the neutrino beam of the CERN SPS' and the CERN Courier says the first SPS neutrino beams appeared early in 1977; the page's December 1976 is kept as the experiment's own statement. In 1983 the detector was split in two parts for a neutrino-oscillation experiment in the PS neutrino beam (Dore).
intervals.quote: The experiment took data in the CERN neutrino beams from December 1976 until 1984.

name: CDHS detector
notes: Dore (EPJ H 37, 2012): circular magnetised iron plates interspersed with drift chambers, total mass 1250 tonnes.

placements.note: Approximate: no fetched source gives a coordinate or a hall for this detector in the SPS West Area, so the existing campus-grade point of the CERN Meyrin site (precision 500 m) is used.
placements.quote: The CDHS neutrino experiment at CERN was a collaboration of CERN, Dortmund, Heidelberg and Saclay (later joined by Warsaw) led by Jack Steinberger.

module_count.quote: It consisted of 19 magnetized iron modules, separated from each other by wire drift chambers.

total_mass.quote: The detector had a mass of 1250 tons and combined the functions of a muon spectrometer and hadron calorimeter.

summary.plain: A stack of magnetised iron slabs with tracking chambers between them: neutrinos strike the iron, and the chambers follow the muon and the hadron shower that come out.
summary.technical: 1250 t iron-plate (toroidal) spectrometer/calorimeter of 19 magnetised iron modules separated by wire drift chambers; a 31 m^3 liquid-hydrogen target was later placed in front to study neutrino interactions in hydrogen.

technology.quote: It consisted of 19 magnetized iron modules, separated from each other by wire drift chambers.
technology.value: Magnetised iron modules separated by wire drift chambers, serving as muon spectrometer and hadron calorimeter
